Resolved the two design residuals routed by the plan reconciliation. RF-070-001-01 (spec AUTH-011 vs design Security conflict): took option (a) and specified a concrete session-bound anti-CSRF mechanism in a new design.md section '## Cross-Site Request Forgery Protection' — a stateless signed double-submit proof bound to the browser-session PASETO jti/sub/aud via HMAC under a dedicated fail-loud csrf_signing_key (no schema, no per-request DB read), layered on a trusted-Origin check, delivered through a non-authenticating smackerel_csrf companion cookie plus a _csrf form field and a csrf-token meta tag, echoed via _csrf/X-CSRF-Token, enforced for every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE by a MutationTrustGuard across server-form/HTMX/PWA/JSON/Cards/admin with a pre-session variant for login/registration/logout. Reconciled the contradictory 'No token is exposed for a custom CSRF scheme' statement to necessary-not-sufficient SameSite plus a required session-bound proof, and clarified the proof is not session material so the HttpOnly session PASETO stays script-inaccessible. RF-070-001-02: extended the design Testing And Validation Strategy table to SCN-070-001-09/10/11. Supporting internal-consistency edits: MutationTrustGuard foundation contract, foundation-owned CSRF behavior, anti-CSRF proof-carrier variation axis, companion-cookie cross-reference, a 403-before-mutation failure-mapping row, a csrf telemetry line, two rejected-alternative subsections, and a complexity-tracking row. AUTH-011 was upheld (not weakened); the mechanism matches the already-planned SCOPE-05 surface (MutationGuard, csrf middleware/enforcement test files, and the origin_rejected|csrf_missing|csrf_stale|csrf_mismatch|accepted plus family telemetry vocabulary), so no scope/test/DoD re-reconciliation is required.
